topic: The Geometry of Light: Dandelin Spheres and Conic Sections
target_audience: High school geometry or early undergraduate students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Cutting Plane
lecture_lines: Conic sections arise from cutting a double cone.
Changing the cutting angle alters the shape produced.
Shapes include circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.
animations: Show a 3D double cone [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg] with a flat plane cutting it. (#FFFFFF)
Rotate the plane to change the intersection shape. (#FFFF00)
Display the resulting circle, ellipse, parabola, and hyperbola derived from the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg]. (#00FF00)

sections.title: Introducing the Dandelin Spheres
lecture_lines: A Dandelin sphere is placed inside the cone.
It is tangent to both the cone and plane.
This tangency point links geometry to the curve.
animations: Place a sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] inside the cone [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg], touching the cone surface. (#00FFFF)
Slide a plane [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/plane.svg] until it touches the sphere and cone. (#FF00FF)
Highlight the point where plane [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/plane.svg] and sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] touch. (#FF0000)

sections.title: The Mathematical Magic: Proving the Ellipse
lecture_lines: Points on the curve satisfy a distance property.
Distances to tangency points are constant for ellipses.
This creates the definition of an ellipse.
The sphere tangency points act as the foci.
Geometry explains why the ellipse is formed.
animations: Draw a point P on the ellipse. (#FFFFFF)
Show distances from P to the two tangency points. (#FFFF00)
Demonstrate that the sum of these distances is constant. (#00FF00)
Label the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] tangency points as the two foci. (#FF00FF)
Outline the ellipse showing the focus-sum property. (#00FFFF)

sections.title: Connecting Shapes to Spheres
lecture_lines: Adding a second sphere generalizes the proof.
Parabolas use one sphere in the cone.
Hyperbolas use spheres in different cone nappes.
animations: Add a second [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] above the cutting plane. (#FF8000)
Show the parabola formed with one [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg]. (#00FF00)
Show the hyperbola with [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg]s in opposite nappes. (#FF0000)

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Synthesis
lecture_lines: Dandelin spheres connect abstract and physical properties.
Foci and directrix emerge from this logic.
